questions.stem: What happened in New York's Prospect Park on Tuesday?
options: A) Many facilities were destroyed by a wandering cow.
B) A wandering cow knocked down one of its fences.
C) Some tourists were injured by a wandering cow.
D) A wandering cow was captured by the police.

explain.定位:
New York City police captured a cow on the loose in Prospect Park on Tuesday after the
animal became an attraction for tourists while walking along the streets and enjoying the
park facilities.
纽约市警方周二在展望公园（Prospect Park）捕获了一头走失的牛，此前这头牛在街上游
荡、在公园设施间穿行，成了游客眼中的一大看点。
explain.信号:
新闻首句即主事件。答案信号是"新闻首句"：四级短篇新闻的核心事件几乎总在开头第一句
交代。本篇开门见山 New York City police captured a cow on the loose in Prospect
Park on Tuesday，主语+谓语+宾语就是事件主干，听到这句就该锁定第 1 题。
explain.替换:
New York City police captured a cow on the loose ↔
A wandering cow was captured by the police
主被动转换+同义改写
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音只说牛 enjoying the park facilities（在公园设施间穿行、享用设施），A 盗用了
facilities 这个原词，却把"穿行其间"夸大成 Many facilities were destroyed（许多设施被
毁坏）。原文从未说设施被破坏，属听到 facilities 就误选的陷阱。
借用原文：enjoying the park facilities
B) 张冠李戴
录音说牛 knocking down a police officer in the process（过程中撞倒了一名警察），B
盗用了 knocking down 这个原词，却把被撞的对象偷换成 one of its fences（一处围
栏）。撞倒的是"人"不是"围栏"，属张冠李戴式的对象偷换。
借用原文：knocking down a police officer in the process
C) 未提及
录音说牛 became an attraction for tourists（成了游客的看点），C 盗用了 tourists 这个
原词，却凭空编出 tourists were injured（游客受伤）。原文通篇没提任何人受伤，属听到
tourists 就联想到"出事受伤"的无中生有。
借用原文：became an attraction for tourists

questions.stem: What do we learn about the cow from the end of the news report?
options: A) It was shot to death by a police officer.
B) It found its way back to the park's zoo.
C) It became a great attraction for tourists.
D) It was sent to the animal control department.

explain.定位:
Police turned it over to the animal control department after they caught it.
警方抓住这头牛后，把它移交给了动物管制部门。
explain.信号:
全文最后一句即结局。答案信号是"录音最后一句"：题干既然问 from the end，落点就在
收尾句 Police turned it over to the animal control department。这是全篇对牛最终去向
的交代，正是结局题该抓的那一句。
explain.替换:
Police turned it over to the animal control department ↔
It was sent to the animal control department
短语同义+主被动转换
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音说警察 shot an arrow to put it to sleep（射了一支箭把牛麻醉睡着），A 盗用了
shot 这个原词，却把"射麻醉箭让它睡着"曲解成 shot to death（射杀致死）。牛是被麻醉
运走、并非被打死，属听到 shot 就联想到"打死"的陷阱，也与原文事实相反。
借用原文：shot an arrow to put it to sleep
B) 未提及
录音说牛被麻醉后 they loaded the cow into a horse trailer（被装进马拖车运走），且 It
was not clear where the cow came from（连牛从哪来都不清楚），根本没有"自己找回
动物园"一说。B 的 found its way back to the park's zoo 属原文未提及、且与"被人装
走"相反的编造。
借用原文：they loaded the cow into a horse trailer
C) 答非所问
录音确实说牛 became an attraction for tourists（成了游客的看点），C 几乎原句照搬，
极具迷惑性。但题干问的是 from the end of the news report（结尾），"成景点"出现在
报道开头、是事件起因/过程，不是结尾交代的结局，属答非所问。
借用原文：became an attraction for tourists
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Starting April 28th of this year, the National Museum of Natural History will begin renovating its
fossil hall. The fossil hall, which displays some of the world's oldest and largest fossil specimens,
receives more than 2 million visitors each year. It's one of the museum's most famous attractions. As a
result, the museum plans to expand the hall as well as add to its ancient birds collection. Bird lovers,
both young and old, have already responded with excitement at the news. The museum's social media
account has been flooded with messages of support. In the meantime, the current collection will be
closed. However, visitors will be compensated during the closure. The Museum's special exhibition area
will now be free of charge. This week the resident exhibition is a display of ancient wall paintings on
loan from Australia. They celebrate the cultural heritage of the country and will be available to view
until Sunday. Next week the exhibition will be taken over by the Wildlife Photographer of the Year
Competition. The winner of this year's competition will be awarded a preview of the new fossil hall as
well as a cash prize.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the fossil hall of the National Museum of Natural History?
options: A) It is the largest of its kind.
B) It is going to be expanded.
C) It is displaying more fossil specimens.
D) It is starting an online exhibition.

explain.定位:
As a result, the museum plans to expand the hall as well as add to its ancient birds collection.
因此，博物馆计划扩建这个展厅，并扩充它的古代鸟类藏品。
explain.信号:
计划动作句。答案落在表示馆方安排的 the museum plans to expand the hall，plans to
这种交代下一步打算的措辞就是信号：新闻里介绍某机构要做什么时，这种 plan to\will 句
往往就是考点所在。
explain.替换:
the museum plans to expand the hall ↔ It is going to be expanded.
主动变被动同义改写
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念了 some of the world's oldest and largest fossil specimens，含 largest，A
项 It is the largest of its kind. 就盗这个 largest 来骗你；但原文说的是展厅里的化石标本
是最古老最大的，不是说这个展厅本身是同类中最大的，主语被偷换了。
借用原文：some of the world's oldest and largest fossil specimens
C) 原词陷阱
C 项 It is displaying more fossil specimens. 盗用了原文反复出现的 fossil specimens，
让你觉得耳熟就想选；但原文说馆方是要扩建展厅、扩充古代鸟类藏品，并没有说正在展出
更多的化石标本，displaying more 是录音没有的说法。
借用原文：displays some of the world's oldest and largest fossil specimens
D) 未提及
D 项 It is starting an online exhibition. 里的 online（线上）录音里根本没出现；原文讲
的是免费开放特别展区、实体展览轮换，没有任何线上办展的内容，属于无中生有。

questions.stem: What is on display this week in the museum's resident exhibition hall?
options: A) A collection of bird fossils from Australia.
B) Photographs of certain rare fossil exhibits.
C) Some ancient wall paintings from Australia.
D) Pictures by winners of a wildlife photo contest

explain.定位:
This week the resident exhibition is a display of ancient wall paintings on loan
from Australia.
本周，常驻展览展出的是从澳大利亚借展的古代壁画。
explain.信号:
时间标志句。答案句以时间词 This week 起头，直接对应题干的 this week，这种以时间状
语开头的句子就是信号：题目问哪一周，就锁定原文里念到那一周的那一句。
explain.替换:
a display of ancient wall paintings on loan from Australia ↔
Some ancient wall paintings from Australia.
概括等值的同义改写
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
A 项 A collection of bird fossils from Australia. 把原文里 from Australia 这个地名和
birds collection 强行拼在一起；可原文里鸟类藏品是 add to its ancient birds collection
（馆方要扩充的藏品），from Australia 修饰的是壁画不是鸟类化石，是把对的地名安到错
的东西上。
借用原文：add to its ancient birds collection
B) 原词陷阱
B 项 Photographs of certain rare fossil exhibits. 盗用原文反复出现的 fossil 来制造耳熟
感；但录音从没说本周展的是化石的照片，本周展的是壁画，Photographs of…fossil 是录
音没有的拼凑。
借用原文：displays some of the world's oldest and largest fossil specimens
D) 与原文相反
D 项 Pictures by winners of a wildlife photo contest 对应原文的 Next week the
exhibition will be taken over by the Wildlife Photographer of the Year Competition，
但那是下一周的安排；题目问的是 this week，把 next week 的内容拿来当 this week 的答
案，是时间被偷换。
借用原文：Next week the exhibition will be taken over by the Wildlife Photographer of the
Year Competition

questions.stem: What have six birds been trained to do at a French historical theme park?

explain.定位:
Six birds have just been trained to pick up rubbish at a French historical theme park.
六只鸟刚刚在法国一座历史主题公园里被训练去捡拾垃圾。
explain.信号:
首句点题 + trained to 结构。答案就藏在录音第一句：信号是与题干同款的 trained to
pick up rubbish 结构，"trained to" 后面紧跟的动作 pick up rubbish 就是答案；新闻第
一句往往直接交代核心事实，开头就要竖起耳朵。
explain.替换:
pick up rubbish ↔ Pick up trash.
rubbish=trash 同义替换
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音确有 visitors are already good at keeping things clean 提到 visitors，B 项 Amuse
visitors. 就盗用 visitors 这个原词诱你 "听到就选"，但原文说的是游客本就爱干净，从未说
鸟去逗乐游客，答非所问。
借用原文：visitors are already good at keeping things clean
C) 未提及
Deliver messages. 在录音里毫无对应——原文只说捡垃圾、与人 communicate（交
流），从没提送信送消息，属凭 "鸟会送信" 的旧印象臆造，直接排除。
D) 张冠李戴
录音里 play 和 children 确实都出现过——establish a relationship through play 有
play，下文 children 也念到，D 项 Play with children. 就把这两个原词拼成一个录音没说
过的动作。原文说的是鸟通过 play 与 humans 建立关系，并非 "和孩子玩"，张冠李戴。
借用原文：establish a relationship through play

questions.stem: Why were rooks chosen by the park manager?
options: C) They are quite easy to tame.
D) They are clean and pretty.

explain.定位:
He says that rooks, the chosen birds, are considered to be particularly intelligent.
他说，被选中的这种鸟——白嘴鸦——被认为格外聪明。
explain.信号:
the chosen birds + 定性形容词。信号是 the chosen birds（被选中的鸟）这一回指，正
对题干的 chosen；紧跟其后的定性词 particularly intelligent 就是被选原因。听到对某对
象下 "considered to be + 形容词" 的判断，那个形容词往往就是答案。
explain.替换:
particularly intelligent ↔ They are especially intelligent.
particularly=especially 程度词替换
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音后文确有 children 出现（家长担忧那段），B 项 They are children's favorite. 就借
children 这个原词诱选，但原文从未说这种鸟是 "孩子的最爱"，更没把它当作被选理由，答
非所问。
借用原文：some parents are concerned that it encourages their children to drop litter
C) 未提及
They are quite easy to tame. 听着最像挑鸟的理由，但录音通篇没说这种鸟 "易驯服"——
只说它聪明、爱与人交流。这是凭 "挑动物当然挑好驯的" 常识脑补，原文无据，排除。
D) 原词陷阱
录音里 clean 确实出现过——visitors are already good at keeping things clean，D 项
They are clean and pretty. 就盗用 clean 来骗 "听到就选"。但原文的 clean 是说游客爱保
持整洁，与鸟 "干净漂亮" 无关，且 pretty 全篇未提，属偷换 + 拼凑。
借用原文：visitors are already good at keeping things clean

questions.stem: What is the concern of some parents?
options: A) Children may be harmed by the rooks.
B) Children may be tempted to drop litter.
C) Children may contract bird diseases.
D) Children may overfeed the rooks.

explain.定位:
However, some parents are concerned that it encourages their children to drop litter so they
can watch the birds pick it up.
然而，一些家长担心这会怂恿自家孩子乱扔垃圾，好让他们看鸟去把垃圾捡起来。
explain.信号:
转折 However + concerned that。双重信号：先是转折词 However——它之前都是正
面叙述，转折之后才出现负面顾虑；紧接 concerned that 直接点出担心，that 后那句即顾
虑内容。听力里 "However + 担心词" 一出现，答案句基本就锁定了。
explain.替换:
it encourages their children to drop litter ↔ Children may be tempted to drop litter.
encourage→be tempted 主被动+同义
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音多次提到这种鸟（rooks），A 项 Children may be harmed by the rooks. 就盗用
rooks 这个原词，再配上最吓人的 harmed 来诱选。但原文家长的担心是孩子乱扔垃圾，从
未说鸟会伤害孩子，与原文相反方向的臆造，排除。
借用原文：rooks, the chosen birds, are considered to be particularly intelligent
C) 未提及
Children may contract bird diseases. 听起来很像 "接触鸟该担心" 的常识，但录音里
disease/染病只字未提，纯属脑补，排除。
D) 张冠李戴
录音里确有喂食情节——delivers a small amount of bird food，D 项 Children may
overfeed the rooks. 就借 food/喂这个原词诱选。但喂食的是那个机关盒子奖励鸟、与孩
子无关，更非家长担忧，张冠李戴。
借用原文：delivers a small amount of bird food

questions.stem: What do we learn about the TV show Science Nation?
options: A) It will be produced at Harvard University.
B) It will be hosted by famous professors.
C) It will cover different areas of science.
D) It will focus on recent scientific discoveries.

explain.定位:
It will be about science, all sorts of science. Each episode will focus on a different area of
science, and tell us what we know, how we know it, and what we still don't know.
它将关于科学，各种各样的科学。每一集会聚焦科学的一个不同领域，告诉我们已经知道什
么、是怎么知道的、以及还有什么是我们仍不知道的。
explain.信号:
正面陈述节目内容的应答句。男方问 What would Science Nation be about，女方的应答
正面交代节目内容；对话里被问者的直接应答就是答案信号，紧接着的 Each episode will
focus on a different area of science 就是承载答案的那句。
explain.替换:
Each episode will focus on a different area of science ↔ It will cover different areas of science
focus on a different=cover different areas
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 Harvard University 确实出现，但说的是主持人 Professor Susan Paul from
Harvard University——即主持人来自哈佛，不是节目"在哈佛制作"。选项 produced at
Harvard University 偷换成"制作地点"，是听到 Harvard 就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：Professor Susan Paul from Harvard University
B) 与原文相反
录音说 The show will have one host only，只有一位主持人 Susan Paul 教授。选项
hosted by famous professors 盗用了"教授"这个原词，却把"一位"夸成"多位名教授主
持"，与原文数量相反。
借用原文：The show will have one host only
D) 未提及
录音说节目讲 what we know, how we know it, and what we still don't know，是知识的
全貌，并没有限定为"最近的科学发现"。选项 focus on recent scientific discoveries 里的
recent 是录音未提的限定，属于自行加码。

questions.stem: In what way will the TV show Science Nation differ from traditional documentaries?
options: A) It will be more futuristic.
B) It will be more systematic.
C) It will be more entertaining.
D) It will be easier to understand.

explain.定位:
It will be like a documentary in the sense that it will be non-fiction and fact-based. However,
our idea is for it to be also fun and entertaining, something which traditional documentaries
aren't so much.
从它是非虚构、基于事实这点看，它像一部纪录片。然而，我们的想法是让它同时也有趣、
有娱乐性，而这正是传统纪录片不太具备的。
explain.信号:
转折 However 后才是真意。前半 It will be like a documentary 说相同点，是干扰；转折
词 However 之后 fun and entertaining, something which traditional documentaries
aren't so much 才点出与传统纪录片的不同，转折后才是答案落点。
explain.替换:
fun and entertaining, something which traditional documentaries aren't so much ↔
It will be more entertaining
entertaining 同词＋比较义还原
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
录音通篇没说节目更"未来感/前卫"，选项 more futuristic 的特点无任何原文依据，属凭"科
技节目大概很前卫"的常识硬猜。
B) 未提及
录音只说节目 non-fiction、fact-based、fun、entertaining，从没说它更"系统/有条理"。
选项 more systematic 是录音未提的特点，凑数干扰。
D) 过度推断
节目讲科学、要 fact-based，容易让人联想"更好懂"，但录音点出的与纪录片不同之处是
entertaining，而非 easier to understand。该项是顺着"科普应该更易懂"的推断答非所
问。

questions.stem: Who will be the intended audience of the TV show Science Nation?
options: C) Children in their early teens.

explain.定位:
Okay, so it will be both educational and entertaining, and your audience will be anyone
interested in science, right?
好的，所以它将既有教育性又有娱乐性，你们的观众将是任何对科学感兴趣的人，对吗？
explain.信号:
被确认的应答句。男方复述 your audience will be anyone interested in science, right
求确认，女方在 That's correct. Yes 给了肯定；男方复述＋女方确认这一组就是答案信号，
受众信息被双方共同坐实。
explain.替换:
anyone interested in science ↔ People interested in science
anyone=people 范围等值
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
录音说受众是 anyone interested in science（任何对科学感兴趣的人），没限定年龄。选
项 Youngsters eager to explore 擅自缩成"渴望探索的年轻人"，把宽范围偷换成窄人群。
借用原文：anyone interested in science
C) 未提及
录音从没提年龄，更没说是 Children in their early teens（十几岁初段的孩子）。这是
把"科普节目大概给孩子看"的常识硬塞进受众，原文未提且范围被收得最窄。
D) 原词陷阱
选项 Students majoring science 借用了反复出现的 science 一词，却把受众缩成"科学专
业的学生"，而录音说的是 anyone interested in science，是听到 science 就想选的原词陷
阱兼范围收窄。
借用原文：anyone interested in science

questions.stem: What does the woman want the man to do for the TV show?
options: C) Help promote it on the Internet.
D) Make episodes for its first season.

explain.定位:
Basically what we need from you is financial support. In order to go ahead with this idea, we
need two million dollars.
基本上，我们需要你们提供的是资金支持。为了推进这个想法，我们需要两百万美元。
explain.信号:
提出需求的应答句。男方先问 what exactly you want from us，女方应答 what we need
from you is financial support；被问者用 what we need from you is 这种明确提需求的
句式直接点题，就是答案信号。
explain.替换:
what we need from you is financial support ↔ Provide financial support
need from you=provide 同事换说法
we need two million dollars ↔ Provide financial support
two million dollars 即财力支持
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
女方明说需要的是 financial support（资金），而非专业意见。选项 Offer professional
advice 录音从未提及，凭"找专家提案大概要建议"的常识硬填。
C) 未提及
录音通篇没说让男方"在网上推广"。选项 Help promote it on the Internet 是个看似具
体、实则录音未提的动作，属凭空添加。
D) 张冠李戴
录音 making all 12 shows in the first season 里的"制作第一季"是女方这边要用那笔钱去
做的事，不是要男方做的。选项 Make episodes for its first season 盗用 first season、
make shows 等原词，把出钱方与做事方的角色搞反了。
借用原文：making all 12 shows in the first season

questions.stem: How does the man feel about himself?

explain.定位:
M: I feel like I'm a failure. I can't seem to do anything very well.
男：我觉得自己是个失败者。我好像什么都做不好。
explain.信号:
被问者直接自评。女方先问 You don't look very happy.，男方紧接着的应答 I feel like I'm
a failure. 就是答案句——态度题的落点在"被问的人自己说出来的感受"，I feel 后面那句
即是。
explain.替换:
I feel like I'm a failure. I can't seem to do anything very well. ↔ Dissatisfied.
自评失败即对己不满
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Unsure. 是"拿不定主意"，但男方说的是 I can't seem to do anything very well.，态度很
明确就是觉得自己差，不是犹豫不决，方向不符。
B) 偷换概念
Helpless."无助"听起来很贴近沮丧，容易误选，但男方说的是 I feel like I'm a failure.，重
点在"对自己不满"而非"束手无策、求救无门"，语义偏了一档。
C) 原词陷阱
Concerned. 极具迷惑性，因为女方后面确实说了 Over-concern with being perfect can
damage our confidence，concern 这个词在录音里真的出现过。但那是女方分析男方"过
度在意完美"时用的词，不是男方此刻"对自己的感受"，属于听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：Over-concern with being perfect can damage our confidence

questions.stem: What does the woman think is the man's problem?
options: A) He is too concerned with being perfect.
B) He loses heart when faced with setbacks.
C) He is too ambitious in achieving goals.
D) He takes on projects beyond his ability.

explain.定位:
W: But be careful. Over-concern with being perfect can damage our confidence if we never
achieve it.
女：但要当心。过度执着于完美，如果永远达不到，会损害我们的自信。
explain.信号:
转折 But 后是真意。女方先说 that's very admirable 表面肯定，紧接 But be careful. 一
转，转折之后 Over-concern with being perfect can damage our confidence 才是她真
正点出的问题所在——转折词后才是落点。
explain.替换:
Over-concern with being perfect ↔ He is too concerned with being perfect.
Over- 等于 too…
explain.排除:
B) 答非所问
He loses heart when faced with setbacks."遇挫就灰心"听上去符合男方的沮丧状态，但
题目问的是"女方认为他的 problem"，女方点的是"过度求完美"，并未把他的问题归为"遇
挫灰心"，张冠李戴到了男方的表现上。
C) 偷换概念
He is too ambitious in achieving goals."太有野心"看似与男方 I really want to push
harder and progress further 的上进劲对得上，但女方诊断的是"过度求完美"，不是"野心
太大"，二者并非一回事。
借用原文：I really want to push harder and progress further
D) 未提及

questions.stem: How does the man feel when he sees others accomplishing things?

explain.定位:
M: I always feel down when I see others accomplishing things, and I feel miserable about my
own achievements.
男：每当看到别人取得成就，我总是情绪低落，并为自己的成绩感到痛苦。
explain.信号:
情境词与心情词同句。男方 when I see others accomplishing things 这一 when 情境后
紧跟 I feel miserable about my own achievements，情境与心情出现在同一句，正是答
案句——被问者自述、且情境心情同框。
explain.替换:
I feel miserable about my own achievements ↔ Miserable.
原句心情词直接对应
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
Embarrassed."尴尬"，但男方在 I feel miserable about my own achievements 里讲的是
内心痛苦、自惭，不是社交场合的难为情，情绪类型不对。
B) 与原文相反
Unconcerned."不在乎"与男方 I feel miserable"很痛苦"恰好相反。男方明明非常在意自己
不如人，选"不在乎"是把极性弄反了。
借用原文：I feel miserable about my own achievements
D) 偷换概念
Resentful."愤恨"指向对别人的怨恨，但男方 I feel miserable about my own
achievements 痛苦的对象是"自己的成绩"，是冲自己来的失落，不是怨别人，方向不符。

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do?
options: A) Try to be optimistic whatever happens.
B) Compare his present with his past only.
C) Always learn from others' achievements.
D) Treat others the way he would be treated.

explain.定位:
W: You're the only person you should be comparing yourself with. When you compare your
current status with the starting point, you'll find you've made progress.
女：你唯一该比较的对象就是你自己。当你拿现在的状态和起点相比，你会发现自己已经进
步了。
explain.信号:
建议句 should/When you。女方 You're the only person you should be comparing
yourself with. 用 should 给出核心建议，紧接 When you compare your current status
with the starting point 落到具体做法——这正是 suggest 题要抓的建议落点。
explain.替换:
compare your current status with the starting point ↔ Compare his present with his past only.
现在比起点等于今比昔
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
Try to be optimistic whatever happens."无论如何保持乐观"是个泛泛的好心态，听着没
错，但女方的建议落在"只跟自己的过去比"这个具体做法上，并没有说"凡事都要乐观"，过
度拔高成了空泛的口号。
C) 原词陷阱
Always learn from others' achievements."向他人成就学习"极具迷惑性，因为录音里反复
出现 compare、others 这些词，if you always compare yourself with others 还带了
always。但女方的意思恰恰是"别老跟别人比"，选项却说"学别人"，把原意反着用了，是借
原词设的陷阱。
借用原文：if you always compare yourself with others, you'll never feel good enough
D) 未提及
Treat others the way he would be treated."以待己之道待人"讲的是为人处世怎么对待别
人，整段对话谈的都是"如何看待自己、如何比较"，根本没提怎样对待他人，无中生有。

questions.stem: What advantage does the speaker say girls from single-sex schools have over those from coeducational schools?
options: A) They have a stronger sense of social responsibility.
B) They are more likely to succeed in the humanities.
C) They are more likely to become engineers.
D) They have greater potential to be leaders.

explain.定位:
Girls who graduate from single-sex schools are three times more likely to become engineers
than those who attend coeducational schools.
从单性别学校毕业的女生，成为工程师的可能性是上男女合校女生的三倍。
explain.信号:
比较级 more likely than 标出优势句。这句用了 three times more likely to become
engineers than those who attend coeducational schools——'比……更可能'的比较结
构，正面把女校女生与合校女生作对比并点出强在哪，正是题干 over those 要的优势句
信号。
explain.替换:
three times more likely to become engineers ↔ more likely to become engineers
去掉倍数后概括等值
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
录音通篇没说女校女生有更强的社会责任感（social responsibility），They have a
stronger sense of social responsibility. 是凭'女校=更优秀'的印象自行添加的，属无中生
有。
B) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到 humanities，但原句是 In coeducational schools, girls are often
expected to succeed only in humanities or the arts——说的是'合校'女生被局限在人
文，而非女校女生擅长人文。They are more likely to succeed in the humanities. 盗用
humanities 这个原词、却把主角和方向都弄反了。
借用原文：In coeducational schools, girls are often expected to succeed only in humanities or
the arts
D) 过度推断
录音只提到女校女生有 stronger self-confidence, better study habits and more
ambitious career goals，并没有说她们更可能成为领导者（leaders）。They have
greater potential to be leaders. 是从'自信/有抱负'过度引申出来的，属过度推断。
借用原文：stronger self-confidence, better study habits and more ambitious career goals

questions.stem: What do teachers tend to do in coeducational settings?
options: A) Praise girls who like to speak up frequently.
B) Encourage girls to solve problems on their own.
C) Insist that boys and girls work together more.
D) Respond more positively to boys comments.

explain.定位:
Research has also shown that in coeducational settings, teachers are more likely to praise and
give in-depth responses to a boy's comments in class. In contrast, they might only respond to
a girl's comments with a nod.
研究还表明，在男女合校里，老师更可能对男生在课堂上的发言给予表扬和深入的回应；相
比之下，对女生的发言可能只是点头带过。
explain.信号:
场景词 coeducational + 对比 In contrast 标出落点。这句以题干要的场景词 in
coeducational settings 开头，紧接着用 In contrast 把'对男生深入回应'与'对女生只点
头'摆成对照，对比结构正是答案句的强信号，落点在对男生更积极那半句。
explain.替换:
more likely to praise and give in-depth responses to a boy's comments ↔
Respond more positively to boys comments.
praise+in-depth responses 概括为 more positively
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
录音确有 girls are more likely to speak up frequently，但那是描述'女校'里女生的表现，
并非合校老师的做法，更不是老师去'表扬爱发言的女生'。Praise girls who like to speak
up frequently. 盗用 speak up frequently 原词、又把女校现象安到合校老师头上。
借用原文：girls are more likely to speak up frequently
B) 与原文相反
录音说合校老师 more likely to encourage boys to work through problems on their
own——鼓励'男生'自己解决，对女生反而 step in 帮忙。Encourage girls to solve
problems on their own. 盗用 solve problems on their own 原词，却把'男生'换成了'女
生'，与原文相反。
借用原文：encourage boys to work through problems on their own
C) 未提及
录音没有任何老师'坚持让男女生多合作'的内容，Insist that boys and girls work together
more. 是凭'合校=男女在一起'的常识自行编出的，属未提及。

questions.stem: What are teachers more likely to do in an all-girls school?
options: B) Provide a variety of optional courses.
C) Place great emphasis on test scores.
D) Pay extra attention to top students.

explain.定位:
All-girls schools tend to be smaller than coeducational schools, which means teachers will be
able to tailor the materials to girl students' personal learning styles and interest.
女校往往比男女合校规模更小，这意味着老师能够根据女生个人的学习风格和兴趣来量身定
制教学材料。
explain.信号:
场景词 All-girls + 末句收束标出落点。录音末句以题干要的场景词 All-girls schools 开
头，用 which means 引出结论——老师能 tailor the materials 给女生，既是场景对位、
又是篇章收尾的结论句，正是本题答案句。
explain.替换:
tailor the materials to girl students' personal learning styles and interest ↔
Offer personalized teaching materials.
tailor…to personal = personalized
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
录音说的是定制教学材料，从没提供'多样可选课程'（optional courses），Provide a
variety of optional courses. 把'个性化材料'偷换成了'选修课程'，原文无此说法，属未提
及。
C) 原词陷阱
录音确念到女校女生 earn higher scores on their College Board and Advanced
Placement exams，但那是说女生'考分更高'这一结果，并非女校老师'极度看重分数'。
Place great emphasis on test scores. 盗用 scores 原词、却把'分数高'歪曲成'强调分数'，
方向不符。
借用原文：earn higher scores on their College Board and Advanced Placement exams
D) 未提及
录音说老师按每个女生的个人风格定制材料，恰恰是面向全体、因人而异，并没有'额外关照
尖子生'（top students）之意。Pay extra attention to top students. 与录音的个性化精
神相悖，属未提及/与原文相反。

questions.stem: What does the speaker find out about Seattle?
options: A) It often rains cats and dogs.
B) It seldom rains in summer time.
C) It does not rain as much as people think.
D) It is one of the most rainy cities in the US.

explain.定位:
Today I found out that Seattle doesn't really get that much rain compared with most US cities.
今天我发现，和大多数美国城市比起来，西雅图其实并没有下那么多雨。
explain.信号:
开头found out即点题。独白第一句就用 Today I found out that 抛出核心发现，found
out 与题干 find out 直接呼应，这种开门见山的点题句就是细节题的答案落点。
explain.替换:
doesn't really get that much rain compared with most US cities ↔
It does not rain as much as people think.
否定加程度的同义改写
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
It often rains cats and dogs. 借了录音满篇的 rain 制造熟悉感，但 rains cats and dogs
是『下倾盆大雨』，与原文 doesn't really get that much rain 正好相反，听到 rain 就选
会中招。
借用原文：doesn't really get that much rain compared with most US cities
B) 未提及
It seldom rains in summer time. 把雨量少限定到 summer time（夏季），但原文说的是
全年总雨量少、且把雨分散到更多天，从未单说『夏天很少下雨』，属无中生有的限定。
D) 与原文相反
It is one of the most rainy cities in the US. 正是录音要破除的那个误解
（misconception），与开头 doesn't really get that much rain 直接对立，是把转折前的
『大众印象』当成结论选了反向。
借用原文：why does everyone think of Seattle as a rainy city? The primary root of
this misconception

questions.stem: Why do local people in Seattle seldom carry an umbrella?
options: A) They drive most of the time.
B) The rain is usually very light.
C) They have got used to the rain.
D) The rain comes mostly at night.

explain.定位:
This is why few locals in Seattle carry an umbrella generally. When it does rain, it tends to be
a very light rain.
这就是为什么西雅图当地人一般很少带伞。下雨时，雨势往往非常小。
explain.信号:
This is why后接原因。This is why few locals in Seattle carry an umbrella 用 This is
why 标出『带伞少』这一现象，紧接的 it tends to be a very light rain 就是真正原因句，
定位靠这个因果信号而非逐词扫描。
explain.替换:
it tends to be a very light rain ↔ The rain is usually very light.
几乎原句的轻微改写
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They drive most of the time. 听上去像个合理理由（开车就不用伞），但原文通篇没提当
地人开车出行，属凭常识补出来的无中生有。
C) 过度推断
They have got used to the rain. 借了录音的 rain 制造熟悉感，且『习惯了』听起来顺理
成章，但原文给的原因是雨小（very light），从没说当地人是因为『习惯』才不带伞，属
顺着惯性想多了的过度推断。
借用原文：When it does rain, it tends to be a very light rain
D) 未提及
The rain comes mostly at night. 自造了一个『雨多在夜里下』的时间细节，原文只说雨
小、雨分散在更多天，从未说雨集中在夜间，属无中生有。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say Seattle is a good place to be?
options: A) It has a lot of places for entertainment.
B) It has never seen thunder and lightning.
C) It has fewer cloudy days than any other coastal city.
D) It has mild weather both in summer and in winter.

explain.定位:
So in short, if you like sunny but not too hot summers, mild winters but with lots of cloudy
days, Seattle's the place to be.
所以总而言之，如果你喜欢阳光充足但不太热的夏天、温和但多云的冬天，那西雅图就是你
该去的地方。
explain.信号:
in short引出总结。So in short 是结尾的收束信号，其后列出 sunny but not too hot
summers 与 mild winters，正是说话人给出的『好地方』理由，定位靠这个总结信号。
explain.替换:
sunny but not too hot summers, mild winters ↔
It has mild weather both in summer and in winter.
分述夏冬概括为全年温和
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
It has a lot of places for entertainment. 说有很多娱乐场所，但全篇只讲天气，从没提娱
乐设施，属无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱
It has never seen thunder and lightning. 借了原文的 thunder 制造熟悉感，但原文说
Seattle gets an average of a mere seven days a year with thunder——是『很少打雷』
而非 never（从不）；选项把程度推到绝对，属夸大失实。
借用原文：Seattle gets an average of a mere seven days a year with thunder
C) 原词陷阱
It has fewer cloudy days than any other coastal city. 借了原文 cloudy 一词，但原文说
mild winters but with lots of cloudy days——是『多云天很多』，选项却说『比任何沿
海城市云都少』，方向相反，且 than any other coastal city 这个比较原文根本没有，属与
原文相反＋无中生有。
借用原文：mild winters but with lots of cloudy days

questions.stem: What does the German professor say about muscle soreness?
options: A) It occurs when people are doing a repetitive activity.
B) It results from exerting one's muscles continuously.
C) It happens when people engage in an uncommon activity.
D) It comes from straining one's muscles in an unusual way.

explain.定位:
According to a German professor, the soreness comes from straining your muscles in an
uncommon way, for example, jumping on a bicycle for a ride, because you haven't ridden in a
long time.
据一位德国教授所说,这种酸痛来自以一种不寻常的方式拉伸你的肌肉,比如说,因为你很久没
骑车了,却跳上自行车去骑一程。
explain.信号:
人物标志词 According to a German professor 引出结论。答案句由 According to a
German professor, the soreness comes from straining your muscles in an
uncommon way 引出——题干问的正是 German professor 说什么,录音里这个人物标志
词一出现,其后那句 the soreness comes from… 就是承载答案的结论句。
explain.替换:
the soreness comes from straining your muscles in an uncommon way ↔
It comes from straining one's muscles in an unusual way.
uncommon 与 unusual 同义替换
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
It occurs when people are doing a repetitive activity. 说酸痛发生在做"重复性"活动时,而
录音明说成因是 in an uncommon way(不寻常方式),repetitive(反复)与 uncommon(不寻
常)正好相反,方向错了。
B) 原词陷阱
It results from exerting one's muscles continuously. 借用了录音反复出现的 muscles 来
制造"听到就想选"的熟悉感,但它把成因说成"持续不断地用力",录音讲的是"以不寻常方式用
力",并没有说"持续",答非所问。
借用原文：straining your muscles in an uncommon way
C) 偷换概念
It happens when people engage in an uncommon activity. 盗用了录音里的
uncommon 一词显得很像,但录音说的是"以不寻常的方式(way)用力",落点在"方式",不是"从
事一项不寻常的活动(activity)";把"不寻常的方式"偷换成"不寻常的活动",概念被悄悄换了。
借用原文：straining your muscles in an uncommon way

questions.stem: What happens when muscles are damaged according to the passage?
options: A) Blood flow and body heat increase in the affected area.
B) Body movements in the affected area become difficult.
C) They begin to make repairs immediately.

explain.定位:
When the body realises the muscles are hurt, the response is to increase blood flow to the area
and increase body heat.
当身体意识到肌肉受伤了,其反应就是增加流向该部位的血流量并提升体热。
explain.信号:
条件句 When the body realises the muscles are hurt 后给出 the response。答案句
以 When the body realises the muscles are hurt, the response is to increase blood
flow to the area and increase body heat 出现:题干问的条件(肌肉受损)在 When… 从句
里复现,紧跟的 the response is… 就是"发生了什么"的直接回答,是定位信号。
explain.替换:
increase blood flow to the area and increase body heat ↔
Blood flow and body heat increase in the affected area.
主动 increase 转被动 increase,语序调整
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
Body movements in the affected area become difficult. 听起来像酸痛的常识(酸了就难
动),但录音讲受损后的反应只说了增加血流和体热,从未提到"活动变得困难",属凭常识脑补、
原文没说。
C) 与原文相反
They begin to make repairs immediately. 借用了录音的 repair(修复)一词,但录音明说
But this doesn't happen immediately(修复并不会立刻发生),还说细胞要一天才到位;选项
却称"立刻开始修复",与原文恰恰相反——正是预读时标记的绝对词 immediately 被写反的
陷阱。
借用原文：But this doesn't happen immediately
D) 张冠李戴
They gradually become fragmented. 取自录音里 break down the large muscle fibre
fragments 的 fragment 一词,但录音说的是身体派细胞去"分解"已碎的大肌纤维碎片,主语
是身体的修复动作,不是"肌肉受损后逐渐自行碎裂";把后面修复阶段的内容,安到了"受损时发
生什么"这个问题上。
借用原文：break down the large muscle fibre fragments

questions.stem: How long does it take for damaged cells to heal?

explain.定位:
Repair of damaged cells takes about two days, and afterwards the soreness disappears.
受损细胞的修复大约需要两天,之后酸痛就会消失。
explain.信号:
Repair of damaged cells takes about two days 直接给修复时长。答案句 Repair of
damaged cells takes about two days 把题干问的 damaged cells/heal(对应 repair)与时
长 two days 直接绑在一起,数字题里这种"事项+takes about+时间"的句子就是答案句。
explain.替换:
Repair of damaged cells takes about two days ↔ About two days.

questions.stem: The United States Postal Service has a system to ensure its employees' safety.
questions.passage:
The quiet heroism of mail delivery

A) On Wednesday, a polar wind brought bitter cold to the Midwest. Overnight, Chicago reached a low of 21 degrees Fahrenheit below zero, making it slightly colder than Antarctica(南极洲), Alaska, and the North Pole. Wind chills were 64 degrees below zero in Park Rapids, Minnesota and 45 degrees below zero in Buffalo, North Dakota, according to the National Weather Service. Schools, restaurants, and businesses closed, and more than 1,000 flights were canceled.

B) Even the United States Postal Service (USPS) suspended mail delivery. "Due to this arctic outbreak and concerns for the safety of USPS employees," USPS announced Wednesday morning, "the Postal Service is suspending delivery Jan. 30 in some 3-digit ZIP Code locations." Twelve regions were listed as unsafe on Wednesday; on Thursday, eight remained.

C) As global surface temperatures increase, so does the likelihood of extreme weather. In 2018 alone, wildfires, volcanic eruptions, hurricanes, mudslides, and other natural disasters cost at least $49 billion in the United States. As my colleague Vann Newkirk reported, Puerto Rico is still confronting economic and structural destruction and resource scarcity from 2017's Hurricane Maria. Natural disasters can wreck a community's infrastructure, disrupting systems for months or years. Some services, however, remind us that life will eventually return, in some form, to normal.

D) Days after the deadly 2017 wildfires in Santa Rosa, California, a drone(无人机) caught footage(连续镜头) of a USPS worker, Trevor Smith, driving through burned homes in that familiar white van, collecting mail in an affected area. The video is striking: The operation is familiar, but the scene looks like the end of the world. According to Rae Ann Haight, the program manager for the national-preparedness office at USPS, Smith was fulfilling a request made by some of the home owners to pick up any mail that was left untouched. For Smith, this was just another day on the job. "I followed my route like I normally do," Smith told a reporter. "As I came across a box that was up but with no house, I checked, and there was mail—outgoing mail—in it. And so we picked those up and carried on."

E) USPS has sophisticated emergency plans for natural disasters. Across the country, 285 emergency management teams are devoted to crisis control. questions.stem: What do we learn about Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence?
options: A) It is a robot that can answer students' questions.
B) It is a course designed for students to learn online.
C) It is a high-tech device that revolutionizes teaching.
D) It is a computer program that aids student learning.
questions.passage:
Professor Ashok Goel of Georgia Tech developed an artificially intelligent teaching assistant to help handle the enormous number of student questions in the online class, Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence. This online course is a core requirement of Georgia Tech's online Master of Science in Computer Science program. Professor Goel already had eight teaching assistants, but that wasn't enough to deal with the overwhelming number of daily questions from students.

Many students drop out of online courses because of the lack of teaching support. When students feel isolated or confused and reach out with questions that go unanswered, their motivation to continue begins to fade. Professor Goel decided to do something to remedy this situation and his solution was to create a virtual assistant named Jill Watson, which is based on the IBM Watson platform.

Goel and his team developed several versions of Jill Watson before releasing her to the online forums. At first, the virtual assistant wasn't too great. But Goel and his team sourced the online discussion forum to find all 40,000 questions that had ever been asked since the class was launched. Then they began to feed Jill with the questions and answers. After some adjustments, and sufficient time, Jill was able to answer the students' questions correctly 97% of the time. The virtual assistant became so advanced and realistic that the students didn't know she was a computer. The students, who were studying artificial intelligence, were interacting with the virtual assistant and couldn't tell it apart from a real human being. Goel didn't inform them about Jill's true identity until April 26. The students were actually very positive about the experience.

The goal of Professor Goel's virtual assistant next year is to take over answering 40% of all the questions posed by students on the online forum. The name Jill Watson will, of course, change to something else next semester. Professor Goel has a much rosier outlook on the future of artificial intelligence than, say, Elon Musk, Stephen Hawking, Bill Gates or Steve Wozniak.

Thinking small, being engaging, and having a sense of humor don't hurt. Those are a few of the traits of successful science crowdfunding efforts that emerge from a recent study that examined nearly 400 campaigns. But having a large network and some promotional skills may be more crucial.

Crowdfunding, raising money for a project through online appeals, has taken off in recent years for everything from making movies to producing water-saving gadgets. Scientists have tried to tap Internet donors, too, with mixed success. Some raised more than twice their goals, but others have fallen short of reaching even modest targets.

To determine what separates science crowdfunding triumphs from failures, a team led by science communications scholar Mike Schafer of the University of Zurich examined the content of the webpages for 371 recent campaigns.

Four traits stood out for those that achieved their goals, the researchers report in Public Understanding of Science. For one, they use a crowdfunding platform that specializes in raising money for science, and not just any kind of project. Although sites like Kickstarter take all comers, platforms such as Experiment.com and Petridish.org only present scientific projects. For another, they present the project with a funny video because good visuals and a sense of humor improved success. Most of them engage with potential donors, since projects that answered questions from interested donors fared better. And they target a small amount of money. The projects included in the study raised $4000 on average, with 30% receiving less than $1000. The more money a project sought, the lower the chance it reached its goal, the researchers found.

Other factors may also significantly influence a project's success, most notably, the size of a scientist's personal and professional networks, and how much a researcher promotes a project on their own. Those two factors are by far more critical than the content on the page. Crowdfunding can be part of researchers' efforts to reach the public, and people give because "they feel a connection to the person" who is doing the fundraising—not necessarily to the science.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Mike Schafer's research of recent crowdfunding campaigns?
options: A) To create attractive content for science websites.
B) To identify reasons for their different outcomes.
C) To help scientists to launch innovative projects.
D) To separate science projects from general ones.
questions.passage:
Thinking small, being engaging, and having a sense of humor don't hurt. Those are a few of the traits of successful science crowdfunding efforts that emerge from a recent study that examined nearly 400 campaigns. But having a large network and some promotional skills may be more crucial.

Crowdfunding, raising money for a project through online appeals, has taken off in recent years for everything from making movies to producing water-saving gadgets. Scientists have tried to tap Internet donors, too, with mixed success. Some raised more than twice their goals, but others have fallen short of reaching even modest targets.

To determine what separates science crowdfunding triumphs from failures, a team led by science communications scholar Mike Schafer of the University of Zurich examined the content of the webpages for 371 recent campaigns.

Four traits stood out for those that achieved their goals, the researchers report in Public Understanding of Science. For one, they use a crowdfunding platform that specializes in raising money for science, and not just any kind of project. Although sites like Kickstarter take all comers, platforms such as Experiment.com and Petridish.org only present scientific projects. For another, they present the project with a funny video because good visuals and a sense of humor improved success. Most of them engage with potential donors, since projects that answered questions from interested donors fared better. And they target a small amount of money. The projects included in the study raised $4000 on average, with 30% receiving less than $1000. The more money a project sought, the lower the chance it reached its goal, the researchers found.

Other factors may also significantly influence a project's success, most notably, the size of a scientist's personal and professional networks, and how much a researcher promotes a project on their own. Those two factors are by far more critical than the content on the page. Crowdfunding can be part of researchers' efforts to reach the public, and people give because "they feel a connection to the person" who is doing the fundraising—not necessarily to the science.
